newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie seesaws as market feels out range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie seesaws as market feels out range.

text.p: *Range reaffirmed in a seesaw session which saw AUD bid up to $0.7420 only to be slapped back to $0.7370 by fresh offers
*Market confused on where AUD goes from here and interbank players reduced to hunting stops in both directions
*Charts bearish while under $0.7440 and analysts tipping test of $0.7340 with a risk of new year lows

"I wouldn't be surprised if that old chestnut about a strangle option makes an appearance," he said, referring to recurring rumours a well known Asian bank has a habit of establishing huge strangle option positions -- essentially a bet the dollar will stay in a certain range.
By 8.30 am (2230 GMT) the dollar was leaning on support at US$0.7373/78 compared to a finish Tuesday of US$0.7392/97.

Analysts said the technical outlook was bearish while it remained under US$0.7440 and expected a tilt at US$0.7340/50 support soon. A breach there would see it back to the 18-month low of US$0.7310 and risk a new downtrend phase to US$0.7250.

The move lower could come Thursday if crucial employment data prove weaker than expected, something it has made a habit of in recent months. It was a shock 40,300 fall in jobs for May that convinced the market a fifth rate cut was on the cards and the upcoming numbers would have to at least meet forecasts to avoid talk of a sixth.

Market estimates centre on a jobs rise of around 25,000 in July, but that would only make up for past losses and still see unemployment edge up to 8.6 percent from June's 8.5. Analysts did caution that a big jobs gain was statistically overdue and a rise of 50,000 or more could cause a sharp short covering rally.

Elsewhere, the Commodity Research Bureau index ended a strong rally with a 1.66 point fall to 243.60 and analysts looked for further losses in the short term as the market corrected an overbought position. It had climbed almost six percent since hitting a two year low at 232.01 on July 7.

On the crosses the A$ zoomed above 1.3900 marks for the first time since August 1991 after the Bundesbank passed up on a chance to fire a warning shot about the mark's weakness. Profit taking pulled the A$ back to 1.3871/86 but that was still well up on Tuesday's 1.3808/21. It also firmed to 87.99/09 yen from 87.62/72. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
